title: Gastrostomy/Gastrojejunostomy/Jejunostomy Tube Placement
summary: Gastrostomy/gastrojejunostomy tube placement guidance for long-term enteral nutrition, dysphagia, aspiration risk, gastroparesis, and failed gastric feeding.
provenance: Imported from procedure orders PDF updated 4.15.26
reviewNotes: Confirm high bleeding risk classification with local policy.
Confirm anticoagulation hold times with the final table.
Confirm barium and NG tube workflow.
Confirm POD1 clearance and nutrition consult workflow.

items: Confirm sedation plan - patient can lie flat.
Long-term enteral nutrition with inadequate oral intake.
Persistent dysphagia.
Planning for oropharyngeal surgery.
Gastric feeding not tolerated.
High aspiration risk.
Gastroparesis.
Gastric outlet obstruction.
Failed G-tube.
Platelets >50k.

blocks.text: High bleeding risk; hold anticoagulants/antiplatelets per policy.

items: High bleeding risk.
Warfarin: hold 5 days and confirm INR <= 1.8.
IV unfractionated heparin: hold 4-6 hours and check aPTT or anti-Xa.
Enoxaparin: hold 1 dose if prophylactic; hold 2 doses or 24 hours if therapeutic.
DOACs: use agent- and CrCl-specific timing in the anticoagulation table.
Clopidogrel: hold 5 days.
Aspirin: hold 3-5 days.

blocks.text: Moderate or general anesthesia; general is common due to dysphagia indication.

items: Moderate or General.
More often than others, these patients need general due to placement for dysphagia.

blocks.text: Confirm target skin site is usable.

items: Target skin site without active infection or overlying medical machinery, such as leads, pacers, etc.

blocks.text: Confirm indication, imaging, labs, access window, NPO status, barium, NG tube if inpatient, and antibiotics.

items: Confirm indication and review imaging.
Labs are appropriate.
Appropriate window on imaging.
Patient is NPO if moderate sedation.
Barium order to be administered ENTIRE bottle the night prior.
NG tube in place if inpatient.
Ancef 2 g if <120 kg, 3 g if >120 kg.
an accessible anterior gastric body apposed to the abdominal wall.
transverse colon, small bowel, left hepatic lobe, and abdominal-wall vessels.
major vessels follow the curvatures; choose a safe body-wall puncture site.
keep the retention device inside the stomach without obstructing the outlet.
prior surgery, ascites, or a high stomach may change or eliminate the safe window.
Review imaging and identify the stomach, colon, liver, and access trajectory.
Confirm antibiotics and airway plan; insufflate through a verified gastric catheter.
Reassess the window after distention; place gastropexy anchors for the selected technique.
Confirm intragastric needle position, then secure a guidewire in the lumen.
Dilate over the wire; position and deploy the retention device inside the stomach.
Check contrast filling without leak; avoid excessive tension and document feeding clearance and anchor care.
no safe window means no puncture; reposition or choose another approach.
confirm access before dilation and tube position before use.
avoid visible vessels; promptly assess bloody output, expanding hematoma, or instability.
stop feeds and urgently assess severe pain, guarding, fever, or displacement. No blind reinsertion.
gastric access does not remove aspiration risk; monitor airway and tolerance of insufflation.
avoid overtight bolsters or anchors; assess skin pain, erythema, and purulence.

blocks.text: Diet hold until IR clearance, vitals, pain control, pull-type antibiotic course, feeding clearance, and follow-up.

items: POD1 check with no signs of peritonitis.
Flushes without resistance or pain.
Nutrition consult.
6 month routine exchange for balloon retention device.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: No diet until cleared by IR on POD1.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.
IF PULL TYPE: 500 mg Keflex BID x 5 days.

blocks.title: Once cleared by IR
items: Feeding tube: PEG and G Tube diet.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: resume the day after the procedure; bridging requires individualized multidisciplinary planning.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours after the procedure.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours after the procedure.
Apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, and edoxaban: Table 6 lists 24 hours; confirm renal function and local policy before restarting.
Clopidogrel: 6 hours after the procedure for a 75-mg dose or 24 hours for a 300-600-mg loading dose.
Ticagrelor, prasugrel, and aspirin: resume the day after the procedure.
Restart only after procedural bleeding risk is controlled; traumatic, neuraxial, multi-agent, and high-thrombosis-risk cases need individualized review.
